results.oneLine: Meera/Maya Hinglish AI companion (chat, Gemini Live voice, screen-watch, memory graph, games, Capacitor APK) built on top of a reusable, heavily measured "RelationalOS" layer: one prompt compiler, persona modules, a surface contract, predicate safety, a turn trace, a failure ladder and a CI-validated context/ memory system. Both branches are identical at 3a921798 (2026-08-25).
results.product:
Meera (display name "Maya") ships as a Vercel web app plus a Capacitor Android APK with signed OTA web-bundle updates. It has:
- text chat with burst pacing
- a realtime speech-to-speech call on gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview, with a cascade STT-LLM-TTS fallback
- screen-share co-watching driven by a geometry-only scene detector
- games through a generic activity seam
- push notifications
- Telegram (live) and Discord/WhatsApp (code-complete) surfaces

Memory is a Neon Postgres graph: episodes as citation ground truth, cited facts, relational state, and halfvec embeddings, with a nightly consolidation job. The relational layer only got real rows from 2026-08-20, because the cron had never been scheduled before then.

A second persona (Kabir) passes the full invariant floor (412/412), which shows the OS/persona split works. Several lanes, for example Azure-first attachments, are wired and gated but have not been measured live. The research arm (model-swap identity test) is blocked because no affordable judge qualifies.
results.stack: React 19 + Vite 8 + TypeScript 6 client. Capacitor 8 Android with Java twins of the voice and watch engines. Vercel serverless api/*.js (plain ESM). Neon Postgres over SQL-over-HTTP, with halfvec(1536) person-filtered exact scan. Supabase for auth and photos. Models: gemini-3.6-flash brain (free Gemini key pool, then OpenRouter, then Azure), gemini-3.1-flash-live for voice, Gemini TTS, and Azure Foundry grok-4-1-fast-reasoning (extraction), text-embedding-3-small and grok-4-20-non-reasoning (attachments and last-resort chat). GitHub Actions for CI, cron consolidation and APK build. esbuild engine bundle (api/_engine.gen.js) shared by server surfaces.

It adds the 2026-08-25 hardening wave, the Oct-04 password gate and forget-requires-asking incident fixes, plus two lines that diverge: a partial-forget episode-integrity fix (codex branch) and maya.vyakti.ai preview tags (claude branches).
results.product:
Maya (formerly Meera) is a Hinglish AI companion. She texts, takes live Gemini voice calls, watches the screen during calls, plays chess and tic-tac-toe, and keeps a memory graph. She runs on web and a Capacitor Android app, and is now served at maya.vyakti.ai.

This line adds:
- a never-internals safety floor plus a deterministic output fence
- a 208-attack behavioral battery
- chess gamefeel fixes (board-truth fence, adaptive strength, weighted opening variety)
- explicit Google cachedContents, measured at -77%, behind a paid lane that is flag-gated and off
- a revived ops event stream
- a DPDP memory-consent screen with an append-only ledger (migration 016 pending)
- a shared-password server gate (live in production since Oct 5)
- forget-requires-asking, after a model marker irrecoverably deleted 44 rows of a call

The codex branch's partial-forget episode-integrity SQL fix passed CI but is not deployed. It is also not merged with the claude branches' previews commit; the two lines diverge from 11f213ae, the production commit. The Play Store launch is deferred and the forget-retention policy is still open.
results.stack: React + TypeScript (Vite) client with a Capacitor Android shell. The engine in src/engine is bundled into api/_engine.gen.js. Server is Vercel serverless functions in plain JS ESM. Data is Neon Postgres over SQL-over-HTTP (no transactions); Supabase handles auth and photos only. Models: a Gemini free-key pool, an optional paid Gemini key, OpenRouter, and Azure Foundry (grok-4-20 for fallback and vision, grok-4-1-fast for memory extraction, text-embedding-3-small); calls use Gemini Live and Gemini TTS. Node .mjs eval harnesses and a context/ markdown+graph memory system.

techAssets.name: Upstream failure ladder + lane order
techAssets.what: A single classifier sorts upstream failures into quota, transient, deterministic or empty_200. Transient failures get a same-key retry with jittered backoff and a hard wall-clock deadline. Lane order lives in visible constants, and with the flag off the original frozen array is returned by identity.

techAssets.name: Explicit prompt-cache manager
techAssets.what: Explicit Google cachedContents keyed by a SHA-256 of the core bytes. TTL acts as garbage collection, refreshes are rate-limited, and a dead cache name is recreated before falling back to an uncached call. Live-verified at -77%.

techAssets.name: Internals disclosure fence
techAssets.what: A deterministic output predicate for three severe disclosure shapes: confirmation, volunteered vendor name, and architecture claim. It allows one re-draft and has documented cases where it must not fire. Offline: 2/2 severe cases caught, 0 false positives across 205 replies.

techAssets.name: Loop/repeat fence
techAssets.what: A pure function of the transcript that detects topics she over-raises (signal: she uses the word, he does not; no stoplist) and near-duplicates of her own replies (Jaccard 0.8). Allows one re-draft and arms the next turn on streamed lanes.

techAssets.name: Behavioral attack battery
techAssets.what: 208 attack turns, including Hinglish twins, run through the real compiled prompt. Predicate graders with severity tiers, a cash cap enforced before each call, a --dry mode that makes zero model calls, and gate-shaped exit codes.

techAssets.name: Verified-human-intent for destructive LLM actions
techAssets.what: userAskedToForget requires a delete-class word from the user in this turn or the 90s burst before it, in Latin or Devanagari script, before honoring the model's [forget] marker. claimsDeletion scrubs any reply line that claims a deletion happened. 44 checks.

techAssets.name: Partial-forget episode integrity CTE
techAssets.what: One SQL statement that unlinks the surviving raw log rows, inserts content-free provisional wake episodes so the consolidator re-segments them, then deletes the doomed episodes. Passed CI; codex branch only.

techAssets.name: Shared-password server gate
techAssets.what: An HMAC token derived from the access word(s). Off when the env var is unset; changing the word revokes every token. One client fetch wrapper; an eval asserts the protected and open route lists.

techAssets.name: Ops event stream
techAssets.what: A server ops event writer that never throws and records only counts, labels and decisions (never text), into meera_diag scope ops. Comes with the lesson that the path is not proven until a row has been read back.

techAssets.name: Append-only consent ledger
techAssets.what: A DPDP memory-consent table with no update path: the newest row is the current answer, and no column can hold anything a person said. Comes with a warm consent UI and a decline path that closes the memory write gate.

techAssets.name: CharacterSheet / Relational Core split
techAssets.what: Personas are typed fragment fields interpolated into a character-agnostic core. A byte-identity gate and a residue-leak ratchet pinned at 0 guard the split. A second persona (Kabir) passed 412/412 invariants with zero engine changes.

techAssets.name: Single compiler with CORE/TAIL + budget gate
techAssets.what: One prompt assembler for every lane. The safety floors sit in a byte-stable, never-truncated core (also the cache unit), and the volatile tail goes last. The budget gate throws instead of truncating silently.

techAssets.name: Gated surface adapter
techAssets.what: All surfaces (Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord) route replies through one gatedReply call site. A static eval proves no ungated path exists.

techAssets.name: context/ memory system
techAssets.what: Decisions carry reversal conditions; measurements carry n, method and date; rejections are logged; a graph.json index is validated by scripts/context.mjs --check.

techAssets.name: India market and regulatory sweep
techAssets.what: 43-source sweep: Indian voice-agent pricing (₹3-65/min), TRAI outbound-AI rules, DPDP timelines, and companion-category ad policy.

results.oneLine: Vyakti Replica Lab: a consented self-replica control plane (identity/liveness, private evidence processing, provider-neutral VoiceGenome, Azure Personal Voice + self-hosted Chatterbox, blinded voice curriculum, watermark/C2PA provenance, erasure, spend ledger). It is fully built and passes its offline tests, but nothing has been measured live.
results.product: The branch adds a private /studio app where a verified adult enrolls (ID + Azure Face liveness), consents and uploads noisy audio. The audio is scanned, separated, transcribed and turned into reviewable VoiceGenome and evidence-cited Person Model drafts. Voice candidates are auditioned blind through a Bradley-Terry active curriculum and an owner holdout gate with a Wilson bound. A private dialogue lane uses Azure Foundry structured output. Cloned speech can only leave through a disclosure, watermark, signed segment chain and C2PA corridor with a per-segment revocation fence. Every piece is implemented with migrations 015-050, five containerized services with Bicep, and ~35 offline eval suites (16 re-run 2026-10-15, all pass). No Azure Personal Voice request was ever made because Limited Access was not approved. There was no Azure Speech spend, the migrations are not applied in production, there is no evidence the services were deployed, and no voice-quality number exists for any cloning provider. results.oneLine: The 2026-08-26 parallel-workstream wave of Vyakti (Gurukul), a platform for cloning a person's mind and voice. results.product:

results.oneLine: The Vyakti Rooms mainline as it stood at the 2026-09-06 handover: 19 waves (WS-R1 to WS-R140) built past gurukul-ws-as, plus three small Codex takeover commits for Windows portability, fake-payment references and the first-room CLI exit. Nothing was actually "completed".
results.product: Vyakti Rooms lets a creator build an AI replica of themselves in a Studio and publish it as a paid Room (/r/<slug>). Followers reach it through web, PWA, Telegram, WhatsApp or an embed and pay INR 299-599 a month via Razorpay/UPI Autopay. Each follower has a private memory that never reaches the creator or other followers; the creator sees only k-anonymous Pulse counts. Suites are the B2B unit: an organisation owns seats and billing. Everything from waves 1-19 is built and passes the 21-check offline release gate, and migrations through 136 are live on Neon. But the app was never configured live (no NEON_URL or keys on Vercel), Razorpay has never been called, owner voice likeness is unproven, and wave 20 (R141-R150) exists only as briefs. The Codex commits only do takeover hygiene: a product-boundary doc, LF line endings, Windows npm and file-URL fixes, row-keyed fake subscription references, the codex/vyakti-* CI and deploy filters, and a first-room CLI change from process.exit to process.exitCode that stops a libuv crash.
results.stack: Vercel serverless with plain JS ESM (api/*.js thin doors that dispatch to decision modules), Neon Postgres over SQL-over-HTTP (migrations 071-136 for Rooms), and Supabase for auth and storage. React 19 + TS + Vite for studio.html and room.html, with Capacitor for Android. The Room reply LLM is OpenRouter google/gemini-3.6-flash, gated by gatedReply and never-rules. The voice stack is self-hosted on Azure Container Apps T4 GPU behind an HMAC broker; ASR is Sarvam. Payments use Razorpay, messaging uses WhatsApp Cloud API and Telegram, plus web push. The release gate is node scripts/verify-release.mjs (21/23 checks), CI runs on Node 22 and 24, and project memory lives in the context/ graph.

results.oneLine: A 9-Sept-2026 handover snapshot of Vyakti, an Azure-only expert voice/knowledge replica platform. It is one product branch plus a voice GPU-job bake-off branch, a GPU-admission processing branch, and an archive-only history branch, all near-duplicates about 1,030 commits off the 2026-08-25 Meera merge.
results.product: Vyakti ("Feed it -> Meet it -> Deploy it") let an expert upload knowledge and voice and get an AI persona with their voice and scoped per-learner memory, deployable to consumers in Hindi, Hinglish and English. It was Azure-only: Foundry text models, Azure Speech fast transcription and TTS, and serverless T4 GPU on Container Apps, with Neon and Supabase auth. Verified pieces: a synthetic upload passed all 8 Azure processing stages; two Azure GPU Manual Jobs (Chatterbox and VoxCPM2) produced 12 integrity-verified clips; a 7-call memory trial worked for saving, correction and forget. The handover itself says "Not ready for production". There was never a real signed-in journey, owner-voice likeness or human rating, and the one live memory trial failed Hindi language adherence. The authors explicitly admit that defensive infrastructure and bookkeeping crowded out the user journey.
results.stack: React+TS/Vite client (src/studio, src/room); Node ESM Vercel-style API (api/_replica-*, _room-*); Neon Postgres via HTTP with 162 migrations; Supabase auth; Azure Container Apps (Consumption-GPU-NC8as-T4, centralindia) internal GPU app plus Manual Jobs; ACR; Log Analytics as job-output transport; ARM REST 2025-07-01; Azure AI Speech Fast Transcription 2025-10-15 and neural TTS; Azure Foundry text models; Python GPU runtimes (Chatterbox, VoxCPM2).

results.oneLine: The tip of the Vyakti voice-clone platform. It adds a per-account private voice-request batch (persistence only) on top of a full stack of pinned open-weight TTS models running on Azure Container Apps serverless T4 GPUs, with an HMAC broker, a supervised GPU controller and a SQL cost meter.
results.product: A signed-in owner records their own voice in Vyakti Studio and can ask for a private, watermarked sample of their cloned voice saying one fixed Hindi sentence. Before the request is accepted they attest to self-use, and they can rate the result afterwards. The ordinary Chatterbox voice preview did serve production audio in August 2026, but a cold first press needed about 291-293 s to warm. The internal owner-voice CPU service was deployed on 2026-09-14, but it ran no synthesis. Batch 171 (the account-private request) is a table, store, handler and 13 offline tests only. It has no route, no queue consumer and no GPU call, the migration was never applied, and Postgres never parsed its SQL. IndicF5, VoxCPM2, Qwen3-TTS and OpenVoice were each built, deployed and synthesised in isolation and measured on speaker similarity (ECAPA), word error rate (WER) and real-time factor (RTF). No human listening was ever done and no quality winner was declared.
results.stack: Node 24 ESM API and controllers with no framework. Python FastAPI plus PyTorch CUDA GPU runtimes. Bicep for Azure Container Apps (Consumption-GPU-NC8as-T4 workload profile, min 0 / max 1) and Container Apps Jobs. ACR remote builds only, using BuildKit secrets. Key Vault and a user-assigned managed identity hold the HMAC secrets. Azure Blob stores audio. Postgres (Supabase on this branch) holds state, with Supabase auth. Tests are node:test plus bespoke evals/*/run.mjs harnesses. Hosting is Vercel plus an azure-web Container App.

techAssets.name: CPU admission broker to private GPU runtime pattern
techAssets.what: A public FastAPI broker verifies the body HMAC, timestamp skew, nonce replay and size. It probes private runtime readiness and returns a signed 'warming' response while the GPU is cold. Once the runtime is ready, it re-signs the admitted body with a fresh internal timestamp and nonce, so random traffic cannot wake a paid GPU and the signature cannot expire during cold start.

techAssets.name: Supervised Container Apps revision controller
techAssets.what: Calls the ARM REST API to activate and deactivate one exact owned revision, and checks drift, ownership and isolation tags. Close is durable and at most once, admission is revoked before any mutation, and uncertain mutations are never replayed. Requires a supervisor heartbeat lease (30 s) and enforces a 420 s dispatch deadline and a 900 s envelope.

techAssets.name: SQL GPU/provider budget meter
techAssets.what: A microUSD reserve -> in_flight -> accounting_pending/uncertain -> release ledger. It uses an advisory lock per resource and releases only after zero replicas and inactive revisions have been observed. This is the basis for a cost governor that does not rely on lagging Azure Cost Management.

techAssets.name: Azure Container Apps GPU Job controller and supervisor
techAssets.what: Starts, observes and stops ACA Job executions bound to a SQL allocation window, with recovery and observation states. Used for LoRA fine-tune jobs.

techAssets.name: Per-request private grant table pattern
techAssets.what: Composite owner-tuple foreign keys, CHECK-pinned scope receipts, a server-frozen config hash and a snapshot-hash time-of-check/time-of-use guard. Also an idempotent client UUID and a deterministic output path reserved for erasure, with revoke keeping locators. Covers auditable per-action authority in a multi-tenant system.

techAssets.name: Pinned offline open-weight TTS runtimes on ACA T4
techAssets.what: Chatterbox Multilingual V3 (general and Hindi pack), IndicF5, VoxCPM2, Qwen3-TTS (English only) and the OpenVoice V2 converter. Weights are baked into the image with manifest commitments, Hugging Face access is offline at runtime, the spoken AI disclosure is enforced and the PerTh watermark is verified. Responses carry signed receipts.

techAssets.name: IndicF5 Devanagari duration fix and pronunciation normalizer
techAssets.what: Corrects upstream's UTF-8-byte duration estimate, which made Devanagari about 3x too long, using per-codepoint density. A deterministic normalizer emits a reconstructable receipt.

techAssets.name: ACR remote-build wrapper and gated-weight secret build
techAssets.what: Builds an exact-file manifest and plan/run commands for az acr run, quotes arguments safely on Windows and never uses local Docker. Uses a BuildKit secret mount for gated Hugging Face weights.

techAssets.name: Voice-evidence service (ECAPA/x-vector, SepFormer, VAD, DeepFilterNet3)
techAssets.what: A private GPU service with HMAC in both directions. It produces speaker embeddings, speaker separation candidates and denoised candidates for objective voice-similarity gates.

techAssets.name: Voice eval harnesses: sealed blind listening pack and Azure Speech WER
techAssets.what: Opaque-ID blind packs with a sealed key, repeat and attention controls and 4 rating axes, plus a script-aware WER/CER intelligibility scorer that uses Azure Speech.

techAssets.name: Azure Personal Voice provider
techAssets.what: A provider leaf for first-party Azure custom neural voice. Azure-compliant, unlike the ElevenLabs and Sarvam leaves next to it.

techAssets.what: A caller-by-provider matrix that names every non-Azure fallback (OpenRouter, Sarvam, ElevenLabs) and classifies each one before repair.

risks: The branch is 1,262 commits and 2,661 files ahead of main, with 5.8 MB of context logs. The code is dense and minified-style, so reuse means a careful rewrite, not copy-paste.
Batch 171 was never migrated or parsed against live Postgres. One SQL draft already had a USING duplicate-column bug, and the effective Hindi CFG is silently 0 while 0.78 is 'requested'.
Non-Azure provider leaves and fallbacks still exist (OpenRouter, Sarvam, ElevenLabs PVC). Do not import them under the Azure-only constraint.
The code is coupled to the Vyakti schema (vy_replica*, consent, processing artifacts, lifecycle, gpu windows), Supabase auth and Vercel.
IndicF5 weights are gated, and the docs mention a Hugging Face credential once shared in chat, which should be treated as compromised.
Voice cloning needs consent, disclosure and watermarking machinery. A sales voice agent with a cloned human voice carries legal and safety exposure.
No human listening result exists for any model. ECAPA and WER numbers are tiny-n diagnostics, not quality verdicts.
Serverless GPU economics (minutes of cold start, a T4 that is 2-4x slower than real time for frontier models) make self-hosted TTS unsuitable for live calls without an always-warm reservation.

results.oneLine: This is the final Codex checkpoint of the Vyakti replica line. It feeds multimodal evidence metadata (modality, format, locators) into claim extraction and hardens the Group AI layer: portable authority checkpoints, an attributed source selector, truthful delivery receipts and known-consent admission. Its CI gates are green, but the product is unproven.
results.product:
Vyakti is a creator-replica platform. Owned sources become claims with citations, the owner reviews them, and the replica serves private Rooms, Meet, and common-friend groups on Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp.

The branch has two parts:
- **Multimodal (27–29 Sep):** evidence metadata now reaches claim extraction. Text and document evidence keeps UTF-16 locators, audio and video keep transcript timing with limitations, images are not interpreted, the claim schema stays at v2 and the prompt moves to v3.
- **Group AI (30 Sep–1 Oct):** adds the portable turn-checkpoint kernel, attributed recency source selection with a frozen 48-case recall eval, explicit adapter receipts (no false said:true), Telegram sent-time admission only after consent and link instants (enforced in SQL too), and 44 px review targets.

The software contract is accepted at automated scope only: 24/24 release checks on Node 22 and 24, 50 synthetic Postgres groups, and an APK build.

Still open:
- durable dedup (duplicate events produce duplicate model calls and sends)
- dependency-safe forgetting
- native identity link and group UI
- group media
- any live provider or human trial

The owner never answered the replay/retention policy question or the live-trial budget.
results.stack: Plain JS ESM serverless API (Vercel functions) with the channel adapters api/tg.js, discord.js and whatsapp.js behind api/_surface.js. Postgres on Neon with Supabase auth. Azure AI Foundry models with a spend-reservation budget (api/_provider-budget.js). React/TS Studio, Capacitor Android. GitHub Actions runs a 24-check release gate, a keyless synthetic postgres:16.15 SQL job and the APK build. Offline eval registry evals/run.mjs with a network-blocking preload.

techAssets.name: Portable turn-checkpoint kernel
techAssets.what: Dependency-free module that binds scope, policy version, authority snapshot and source snapshot, then re-reads authority, sources, authority, sources before each effect. Invalidation is sticky, DTOs are canonical and frozen, limits are bounded.

techAssets.name: Attributed source-turn selector
techAssets.what: Builds a bounded context packet: 20 mandatory recent turns plus 12 older ones, under a 32 KiB cap measured on the real UTF-8 serialization. Text, span, speaker and episode are kept exactly, and it refuses rather than truncates. Recency is the default and lexical mode is opt-in.

techAssets.name: Frozen preregistered recall eval methodology
techAssets.what: 48 cases: 8 families x EN/HI/code-switch x 2 variants, including an adversarial distractor variant. The corpus hash was frozen before the selector was inspected, and the report gives per-family and per-language receipts.

techAssets.name: Truthful delivery outcome contract
techAssets.what: deliver() validates the whole render before sending, requires an explicit {ok:true} adapter receipt for each fragment and stops at the first failure. Failures raise typed surface_delivery_unconfirmed errors with outcome not_executed or unknown, fragment counts and retrySafe:false.

techAssets.name: Delivery durability / outbox design
techAssets.what: An audit of the duplicate-replay and false-success failures, the receipt semantics of each adapter, and a proposed outbox state machine (prepared/executing/confirmed/not_executed/unknown/cancelled) keyed by transport-event ID plus payload hash.

techAssets.name: Known-consent temporal admission fence
techAssets.what: An inbound message's platform sent-time must be strictly later than group consent and every recipient's link time. The check runs in JS and again inside INSERT...SELECT. Edits, ephemeral messages and business variants are refused, and a microsecond-precise PG timestamp parser is included.

techAssets.name: Telegram group audience witness
techAssets.what: Verifies the current platform audience: bot/admin status, private unlinked chats only, member count plus individual member checks. It is revalidated before egress.

techAssets.name: Multimodal claim-evidence projection
techAssets.what: Normalizes evidence rows for text, documents, audio, video and images, with locators, transcript timing and explicit limitations. It refuses image geometry as meaning and fails closed on partial metadata.

techAssets.name: Source-aware claim review projection + UI
techAssets.what: TS citation DTO validator with modality-specific limitations, plus review CSS with measured 44 px targets and mounted Playwright fixtures.

techAssets.name: Offline research registry / review queue
techAssets.what: Ledger of sources and experiments with review cadences (docs and repos 14 days, papers and standards 90 days). Execution state and outcome are separate fields, and commands are display-only with no fetching.

techAssets.name: Keyless synthetic-Postgres CI job
techAssets.what: A GitHub Actions service container running real SQL-semantics tests for authority predicates, with no production credentials.

techAssets.name: Foundry spend-reservation ledger
techAssets.what: Wraps every paid Azure Foundry call in reserve, begin, mark-uncertain and settle-or-release steps.

techAssets.name: Memory-system adoption research (Honcho, Graphiti, Hindsight, GroupMemBench)
techAssets.what: Patterns to adopt: observer-subject perspectives, explicit vs inferred facts, read-set receipts kept apart from citations, dependency-aware retraction. Also records licence and data-handling blockers.

rejections.tried: Porting the archived GroupAI runtime and context graph wholesale
rejections.broke: It would duplicate authority and still leave the real defect, metadata loss plus Number(null) producing a zero timestamp, unfixed. An additive projection was used instead.

rejections.tried: Bumping the claim schema version to describe modality
rejections.broke: Version-based batch identity would make already consumed evidence eligible again. Only the prompt version (v3) was moved.

rejections.tried: Promoting lexical recall on its pooled gain, or tuning it on the frozen cases
rejections.broke: It recovers 0/27 targets on every adversarial case. Tuning against known answers is not independent progress. Recency stays the default and lexical is opt-in.

rejections.tried: Treating an attempted send, a model reply or an undefined receipt as delivered
rejections.broke: This produced false said:true results and success logs. Ambiguous outcomes must be recorded as unknown and never auto-retried.

rejections.tried: Using arrival time or edit_date as the message time for consent checks
rejections.broke: A delayed message can appear newer than a consent boundary it actually predates. The original sent-time must be used, and the check repeated in SQL.

rejections.tried: Using creator ownership or a private Room session as group-member authority
rejections.broke: Owning the replica is not proof of membership. A verified web account is not proof that it is linked to a Telegram identity.

rejections.tried: Adopting Honcho or Restate as dependencies
rejections.broke: Honcho's server is AGPL, its hosted terms allow fine-tuning and do not guarantee Azure-only processing, deletion leaves derived conclusions, and its scopes are not ACLs. Restate is BSL 1.1. Only the patterns were borrowed.

rejections.tried: Weakening tests to get green (longer timeouts, token allowlists, deleted assertions, fetch monkeypatching)
rejections.broke: That would hide real fixture races and authorization mismatches. Each one was diagnosed causally instead.

risks: Extreme process overhead: context/graph.json is about 31k lines and the docs are dense hedging prose. Most of 1 Oct went on fixture races. Do not import this governance style wholesale.
No idempotency in group dispatch: duplicate webhooks cause duplicate LLM spend and duplicate sends.
The checkpoint kernel is not atomic; a race window remains between assertCurrent() and an external send.
Modules are marked private and UNLICENSED under the @vyakti names and must be renamed for reuse.
Web identity depends on Supabase auth, which conflicts with an Azure/Neon-only target.
The evidence is almost entirely offline or synthetic: no live Telegram, provider-quality, owner-usefulness or deployment proof.
Group commands (/chup, /bolo) were dispatched before the turn guard in the audited source.

results.oneLine: The most complete Vyakti tree (Oct 10-11, 2026): an expert-cloning platform with a Feed/Meet/Deploy studio, published text assistants with one-use access passes, scale-to-zero Azure GPU voice services, and on the codex branch an isolated durable Azure Communication Services auth-email outbox.
results.product: Vyakti turns a creator's material, voice and style into an AI that answers their audience. The creator signs in, feeds it sources (docs, audio, YouTube, WhatsApp exports), meets it (private English/Hindi/Hinglish text rehearsal, the Mirror Call voice loop, a private Hindi voice test), and deploys it as a published text assistant with per-visitor memory, quotas, a budget cap and one-use access passes, or as a follower Room with Telegram/Discord/WhatsApp adapters. The canonical branch's accepted source 32340565 passes 25/25 release gates on Node22 and Node24, but the only deployed web release is the Oct 9 protected Vercel preview. Production migration 173 (access passes) failed its in-transaction catalog assertion and rolled back; it is proven only in a dev DB. The codex branch adds a Vyakti-only magic-link/OTP email lane over native ACS REST with a durable encrypted outbox (migration 174). It is dark behind a flag, has no key bound, and has sent no email. Human sign-in, email delivery, voice likeness, paid conversion and PMF are all unmeasured.

risks: No number here comes from real users or real phones: every echo/barge/EOT figure is from TTS voices and a modelled loudspeaker. Adopt the gates, re-measure the numbers.
Voice Live azure-speech returns empty transcripts on short answers (5/14), which matters for sales calls dominated by 'haan/ok/theek hai'. A second ear for short bursts is needed.
Live-Reference AEC is preview (api-version 2026-07-15); billing of a non-responding stereo session is unverified (possibly +$0.54/h).
gpt-live-transcribe has no logprobs, so any low-confidence gating silently does nothing on it.
429 overflow twin adds +0.3 to +0.9 s and varies by hour; port the fixed one-move overflow logic (r4-duplex/int/r5-rel142), not older copies where hedge twins doubled onto the overflow.
Branch skew: agent.js differs across the three branches (effort low vs none, speculation present or absent); take it from r4-conversation.
Duplex constants (12 dB/80 ms pre-duck, silences, continuer lists) were tuned on child Hinglish, partly in-sample; adult sales callers will differ.
The telephony path is unbuilt: on PSTN/ACS the reference channel must be the agent's outbound TTS stream, and India needs ACS Direct Routing plus a licensed SIP carrier (ACS sells no Indian numbers).
An LLM agent with tools runs ~4-5 s p50 end to end; a serial classify pre-pass costs ~1.8 s and must be parallelised or dropped for a sub-3 s sales agent.

results.oneLine: Taxila's child-facing presentation layer: live lesson content (Forge G1/explainer templates/Studio archetypes/forge3 compose + one tray certificate gate), offline sandboxed codegen (Forge G2 on ACA Jobs), deterministic server-replayed games (Antariksh/Khand 3D on three.js), the token-only Kaksha 'Volt night' design system, and the Asha 2D painted-puppet avatar (lamp1/lamp2 held as failed).
results.product: Taxila's AI tutor shows a live visual in the child's tray while the teacher speaks. The ladder is play level → engine → code template board → skeleton, and every rung is gated at the device's real viewport before it is revealed. On adult-scripted batteries: owner-5 14/14 slots filled, 51 boards with 0 contradictions, and 93% right-artifact-ready in a 200-lesson simulation; request → piece p90 is 5.5 s against a 3 s target. Seven deterministic game families plus the 3D engines Antariksh and Khand grade by replaying signed raw acts on the server, with 0 wrong grades over ≥ 5k random acts per mode. They are in the release, but real-phone fps and the unprompted practice-beat offer are unmet. Kaksha + Volt night has been the default child app for every account since release 11 (2026-10-11): token-only, 120 pages with 0 lint findings, contrast ≥ 5:1. The public site uses the same tokens. Asha's r8 face is live; the newer lamp1 and lamp2 puppets failed blind model-judge gates (uncanny and premium) and are held. No child has used any of this; all numbers are scripted, simulated or software-GL proxy.
results.stack: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite client; three.js (tree-shaken, the only 3D stack); Canvas 2D puppet rig; SVG/DOM whiteboards; plain-JS ESM Node server (one router); zod scene@1 DSL emitting JSON Schema for Azure structured outputs; Playwright/Chromium visual QA; Neon Postgres; Azure Blob; Azure Container Apps (web, worker, untrusted forge-g2-runner Job); Azure OpenAI/Foundry Direct models (taxila-fast, gpt-image-2, gpt-5.6-sol, Kimi K2.6, grok-4-1-fast); Azure Speech TTS visemes; Azure AI Content Safety as one QA layer.

techAssets.what: Every server path that can reveal UI calls certifyForTray/certifyModule at the device viewport before reveal. A test scans server/shared source and fails on any new ungated producer; a mutation check proves the test bites.

techAssets.what: In-Chromium measurement of rendered text px, clipping, overlap and composition fill, including a canvas fillText probe installed via an init script. Runs at named viewports 360/412/1366.

techAssets.name: Closed-enum model 'dress' pattern
techAssets.what: One fast model call may change presentation only through a strict closed-enum schema. The answer is validated field by field (invalid values dropped, never repaired), with a 1.9 s deadline falling back to a code base. No model string reaches the user.

techAssets.name: Forge G1 live personalised fill pipeline
techAssets.what: Pipeline: plan (code) → cache (memory → Neon) keyed by canonical-JSON sha256 over versions + model + kit + item + skin → optional enum-only model flavour (≤ 3.5 s) → code build → code gate → mount. The gate runs before the model call, with a bounded dead-key memo.

techAssets.what: Templates for fractions, number lines, flows, cycles, compare, parts/labels, angle, shape, area grid and bar charts. Every number and position is computed in code, with a strict lint (inside board, no overlapping text) and a truth/guard check against the speaker's line.

results.oneLine: Taxila's quality and release machinery: a sim lab where an AI child with a hidden knowledge key runs whole lessons through the real server and is judged cross-family, a Playwright break-it QA harness, and a gated packaged-tree canary release train with evidence branches.
results.product: These branches hold no product features. They are the machinery that decided whether each Taxila release shipped and whether each teacher change helped. The sim lab (claude/r5-simlab, evals/simlab) is built and was used about 30 times in 36 hours at n=32-64 lessons per arm, with A/A noise checks, model bake-offs, voided runs and a code-decided-outcome child. It is the declared gate for the LLM-agent teacher. The QA harness (claude/r5-qa, tests/e2e) is exploratory and outside CI. It logged 33 defects (2 P0), fixed 14, and exited after two consecutive clean passes, but could not exercise WebRTC in the container. The release train (int/r4-rel8 to rel13.1, then int/r5-rel14x) shipped about 13 releases to Azure Container Apps with per-sha gate stamps, packaged-tree batteries (owner-5 visual requests, round2-content, boards, w2i-safety), a 0% canary smoke, one-PATCH rollback and post-deploy production batteries. The ev/rN-packaged branches are single commits holding only battery output.
results.stack: Node ESM server + React 19/TS/Vite client; Neon Postgres with a dedicated TEST branch for every harness; Azure AI Foundry Direct models via server/azure.js (GPT teacher, DeepSeek-V4-Pro child with Mistral fallback, grok-4-20-reasoning + Kimi K2.6 judges); Azure Speech/gpt-4o-mini-tts + transcriber for the voice lane; Playwright/Chromium for QA; Azure Container Apps (multiple-revision canary) + ACR built from GitHub; Azure Blob for rrweb trace chunks; node:test (~3,100 tests) + tsc + vite build + prompt-budget gate.

techAssets.name: Sim lab (simulated counterparty with hidden-key judge loop)
techAssets.what: Seeded persona cards with a hidden per-skill state and planted misconceptions. A model plays the counterparty, seeing only what a real user sees. Whole sessions run through the real server on a TEST DB. A cross-family judge extracts the agent's belief, code compares it with the card, and the output is failure clusters, FAILURES.md and FACTS.json.

techAssets.name: Decided-outcome simulator mode
techAssets.what: The harness draws each answer's correctness from card state x item depth (seeded answer model). The LLM only voices that outcome, which fixes simulator over-competence.

techAssets.name: Eval lib: cross-family guard, JSON-forcing call, bounded pool
techAssets.what: Throws if the simulator shares a model family with a judge. Includes an askJson with retry and think-tag/fence stripping, and an ordered bounded-concurrency pool.

techAssets.name: Failure taxonomy + deterministic conversation predicates
techAssets.what: 21 typed failure types, an 8-dimension rubric with turn citations, and code checks for repeats, long turns, channel mismatch, pointing at nothing, helpline after disclosure and AI disclosure.

techAssets.name: Eval run hygiene
techAssets.what: Caps parallel sessions on shared deployments with staggered starts, DROPS a run above 2% fallback turns, reuses a judgment only when the transcript lines are identical, and never takes a flag as a value.

techAssets.name: Playwright break-it QA harness
techAssets.what: Production build against the TEST DB. Phone/laptop profiles, Slow-3G + 4x CPU, denied mic, fake mic from Azure-TTS WAVs. Captures console, page errors, HTTP >= 400, uploaded clips and flight-recorder events. Each fixed defect has a PASS/FAIL repro script.

techAssets.name: Defect log format + two-clean-passes exit rule

techAssets.what: Seeded, real-session experience tests. Creates one test account per run and deletes it in finally. The rubric is independent of product code, with an optional strict model judge. owner-5 checks that 12 visual requests produce real stage artifacts, including in the real browser.

results.oneLine: CarbonSettle CommandCentre: a production single-tenant Next.js/Supabase CRM and cold-outbound engine. It has a warmed Gmail mailbox fleet, IMAP inbox with a 14-intent reply classifier, signed per-lead offer pages and PDF briefs, a human-vs-sandbox engagement classifier, ICP scope/EU-export gates and WhatsApp, and it has sent about 9k real emails.
results.product:
CC is the CRM, campaign and lead-gen backbone of an Indian CBAM-compliance firm, run largely by agents. Its parts:
- CRM: leads, pipeline, tasks, activity, calls, imports with audit, hot leads with an AI next action, reports and an investor view.
- Cold-email engine: sequences, A/B subjects, spintax, enrollment-as-queue, mailbox picker, throttle and warmup ramp, placement tests, DNS and Postmaster, suppressions, webhooks.
- Unified IMAP inbox: bounce and warmup filtering, LLM intent classification, translation, AI Reply Studio.
- Prospect chain: signed /p/<token> offer pages with a react-pdf brief, claim capture and heartbeat tracking.
- Other channels: a live but unused WhatsApp Cloud API channel, team chat with Web Push, first-party site analytics and a Capacitor WebView app.

It is live and sending: the October 2026 wave of 2,322 is armed for 19-27 Oct. Tests (14 files, 47/47 claimed) and tsc are reported clean but I did not re-run them. Weaknesses: no tenancy, a shared-password auth gate, about 10 live tables missing from repo migrations, a Supabase Free tier with no backups, and CBAM logic hard-coded in every layer. focused-goldberg adds only a bounce-parser false-positive fix and session docs, and serene-franklin is identical to main.

results.product: It is an operator workspace with 19 sections in 6 areas. The sections cover: company profile; company brain (ingestion with exact-quote review plus lexical RRF Q&A); a thin customers/consent view; an integrations vault (19 adapters, none connected live); and agent studio with immutable versions, release checks and rollback. The rest are campaigns (AI plan, brief, consent preflight, launch, browser call, extracted results), automations (email schedules), conversations, a WhatsApp inbox, follow-ups, an evaluation lab, GroupAI, team, usage and account security. The most complete flow is the campaign: in a fictional workspace, an AI-planned campaign launched, ran a live Azure Realtime browser call and extracted 4/4 result fields. Email, WhatsApp, Telegram and OAuth delivery exist in code but were never exercised against real accounts, and there is no telephony, real CRM/ERP object model or lead generation. Nothing has been hosted: the Container Apps and App Service Bicep is unapplied, and Postgres support is code-only and untested. Everything runs locally on SQLite. Tests are 1153 unit/contract tests with mocked providers, about half of them for voice. There are no e2e or live tests.

results.oneLine: I ran sales-enabler ("Relay") live with local SQLite and real Azure gpt-4.1-mini. It is a working, governance-heavy voice-agent studio with a thin CRM. The flow from signup to public chat runs end-to-end, but the product is the wrong shape for an AI company command centre.
results.product:
Every core flow worked in a live run against real Azure:
- Signup and email verification, done through the dev outbox.
- Company profile saved.
- CSV customer intake: AI column mapping, row review, then apply. This created 4 contacts.
- Brain material: pasted, extracted, then human-approved. Extraction took about 1.3s.
- Business-model offering discovery. It took about 13s and produced 3 offerings and 8 founder questions.
- Agent build: 6 editor tabs, static configuration checks, then release.
- Public Web-chat deployment through a 3-step wizard with mandatory caps, then a public /talk chat. The chat answered from approved facts in 3.2s, not streamed.
- A campaign built through Intent, Audience, Agent and Review. It was correctly blocked at launch because no consent was recorded.

Per view:
- Overview is the best screen, with a clear next action, but it is a setup checklist, not a command centre.
- Company brain has strong evidence-span mechanics but has two separate offering systems and a lossy summary step.
- Customers is a person-only contact card. There is no account, deal, timeline or custom-field support.
- Integrations, Inbox, Automations, Conversations and GroupAI are mostly empty states or need setup.
- Agents is dense, and its test call is blocked without a voice provider. There is no text test in the studio.
- Deployments is solid but long.
- Quality is an internal voice-eval lab.
- Usage & services is honest ops telemetry.
- The account pages and /join are fine.
- /prototype is a simulated concept with the best visual direction in the repo.

No view crashed, no API call returned 5xx, and there is no horizontal overflow at 390px.
